words: يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of yaʾti is the previously mentioned appointed term to which the Resurrection is deferred; on that day no soul speaks except by God’s leave.
rows.anchor: فاعل { يأت } ضمير راجع إلى الأجل السابق الذكر أي يوم يأتي الأجل الذي تؤخر القيامة إليه

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ takes the coming day to mean the Resurrection and requital, with the pronoun referring to them by contextual indication.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم كما في المجمع أن المعنى يوم يأتي القيامة والجزاء

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar reads the day as an indefinite time in which the specified Day arrives; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this as making a time contain itself, and says the distinction between general and specified days does not help.
rows.anchor: وذكر آخرون - كما في تفسير صاحب المنار - أن المعنى في الوقت الذي يجيء فيه ذلك اليوم المعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If day is treated as an event rather than a time, as in the phrase about the Day the Hour rises, its pronoun could refer to the Day without temporal self-containment.
rows.anchor: نعم ربما يؤخذ الزمان متحدا بما يقع فيه من الحوادث فيصير حادثا من الحوادث وتلغى ظرفيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is any one of those present at the gathering, and it can speak only with God’s permission.
rows.anchor: لا تتكلم نفس ممن حضر إلا بإذن الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubled tāʾs in the imperfect of the form tafaʿʿul are commonly and regularly reduced to one.
rows.anchor: وحذف أحد التائين المجتمعين في المستقبل من باب التفعل شائع قياسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment, so the exception concerns the permitted speech rather than which speaker is excepted.
rows.anchor: والباء في قوله { بإذنه } للمصاحبة فالاستثناء في الحقيقة من الكلام لا من المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that a soul says only speech accompanied by God’s permission; worldly people choose what to say whether or not it is legislatively permitted.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا تتكلم نفس بشيء من الكلام إلا بالكلام الذي يصاحب إذنه لا كالدنيا

words: يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s permission governs every event at all times, so this is not exclusive to the Resurrection; it characterizes that Day because its reality becomes manifest there.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرت الصفة أعني عدم تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه من خواص يوم القيامة المعرفة له، وليست بمختصة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other descriptions of the Resurrection likewise express truths that hold always: nothing is hidden from God, no one has refuge from Him, and all command belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أنه تعالى لا يخفى عليه شيء دائما، وليس لشيء منه عاصم دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering removes the veil from people, making realities and the truth of God’s sole power, sovereignty, and command fully evident; worldly causes lose their supposed independent force.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة ظرف يجمع الله فيه العباد ويزيل الستر والحجاب دونهم فيظهر فيه الحقائق ظهورا تاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Day exposes inner secrets, judgment is based on inward states and qualities rather than evidence uncovered through worldly means; what is hidden now becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى يقول فيما يصف هذا اليوم يوم تبلى السرائر الطارق 9 ويقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary human speech uses socially agreed sequences of sounds to disclose meanings hidden in one person’s mind from other people, who cannot perceive those meanings directly.
rows.anchor: والتكلم الذي نتداوله نحن معاشر الناس فيما بيننا إنما هو باستخدام أصوات مؤلفة تدل بنحو من الوضع والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people could directly sense mental meanings, there would be no need to establish languages or speak them.
rows.anchor: لم نحتج إلى وضع اللغات والتكلم بها ولا كان بيننا ما يسمى كلمة أو كلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, an entirely solitary human life would have no speech; worldly life combines the seen and unseen, while a wholly manifest afterlife would not need speech except as disclosure of souls to one another.
rows.anchor: وكذا لو كان النوع الإنساني يعيش في حياته الدنيا عيشة انفرادية غير اجتماعية لم يكن من النطق خبر ولا انعقدت له نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since wrongdoers are recognized by their marks and seized by forelocks and feet, no questioning is needed to identify them on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم فيؤخذ بالنواصي والأقدام الرحمن 41

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Answering the objection from verses where sinners lie, he says people can inspect their own thoughts without speaking, though habitual inner speech or spoken fragments may arise from worldly practice.
rows.anchor: قلت هذا من ظهور الملكات كما أن الإنسان عند التفكير يشاهد خبايا نفسه من غير حاجة إلى أن يخبر نفسه بما يفكر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists and hypocrites may lie because worldly habits appear as traits, but lying cannot deceive God when their insides, records, witnesses, and bodily testimony are exposed; inability to prostrate similarly comes from entrenched arrogance.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء المشركون والمنافقون لما اعتادوا الكذب في نشأتهم الدنيا، وعاشوا على كذبات الوهم ظهر منهم ذلك يوم يظهر فيه الملكات والعادات النفسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the revelation of lying dispositions with the parallel case of people who are called to prostrate but cannot do so; the continuation explains that their established arrogance accounts for this inability.
rows.anchor: وهذا نظير دعوتهم يوم القيامة إلى السجود ثم عدم استطاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is a place of requital, not action: once deeds are done, their consequences necessarily attach to their doer, leaving no human choice in the response there.
rows.anchor: والنشأة الآخرة دار جزاء لا دار عمل فلا خبر هناك عن الاختيار الإنساني وليس هناك إلا الإنسان وعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When summoned, people respond compulsorily, unlike in worldly life when they were called to truth and refused.
rows.anchor: فإذا دعي استجاب اضطرارا، كما قال تعالى يومئذ يتبعون الداعي لا عوج له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any speech in response to questioning is compelled and matches the exposed record; mouths are sealed and limbs testify, so it is unlike voluntary worldly speech.
rows.anchor: اليوم نختم على أفواههم وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون يس 65

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no valid excuse against a necessary requital for completed deeds; an excuse would matter only where the outcome still involved choice.
rows.anchor: فإن العذر إنما يكون في الجزاء الذي فيه شوب اختيار ولتحققه إمكان وجود وعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection speech is not chosen disclosure that may be truthful or false; human choice is lifted there, and speech depends on God’s permission and will, as realities become manifest.
rows.anchor: أن التكلم يومئذ ليس على وتيرة التكلم الدنيوي كشفا اختياريا عما في الضمير بحيث يمكن معه للمتكلم أن يصدق في كلامه أو يكذب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say only morally good speech is permitted because people are compelled to avoid wrong; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the unsupported restriction, since the afterlife is requital rather than a field of action and even excuses are not evil speech.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن معنى قوله { لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } أنها لا تتكلم فيه إلا بالكلام الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects restricting the verse to intercession as unsupported; if it meant only speech for or about another, the wording should specify that relation as the parallel phrase does.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن ذلك تقييد من غير شاهد عليه ولو كان المراد ذلك لكان من حق الكلام أن يقال لا تكلم نفس عن نفس أو في نفس إلا بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses that unqualifiedly deny or affirm individuals speaking are reconciled by the permission stated in 78:38.
rows.anchor: فيه صنفان صنف ينفي التكلم أو يثبته لأفراد الناس من غير استثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses denying all speech, whether true or false, are reconciled by this verse when permission means that afterlife speech is compelled rather than freely chosen.
rows.anchor: وصنف ينفي الكلام على أي نعت كان من صدق أو كذب كقوله هذا يوم لا ينطقون

rows.speaker: صاحب المنار
rows.claim: Al-Manar says the permission clause reconciles verses that absolutely affirm and deny speech; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that it neither distinguishes the two classes nor explains permission in a way that makes the description distinctive of the Day.
rows.anchor: حيث قال في تفسير الآية ونفي الكلام في ذلك اليوم إلا بإذنه تعالى يفسر لنا الجمع بين الآيات النافية له مطلقا والمثبتة له مطلقا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One proposed answer is that speech is allowed at some stations of the Resurrection and prohibited at others; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this still depends on divine permission and reduces to his account.
rows.anchor: وقد يجاب عن إشكال التنافي بوجه آخر وهو أن يوم القيامة يشتمل على مواقف قد أذن لهم في الكلام في بعض تلك المواقف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another answer takes silence to mean absence of speech with a valid argument, though people still confess sins and blame one another.
rows.anchor: وقد يجاب بأن المراد بعدم التكلم والنطق أنهم لا ينطقون بحجة، وإنما يتكلمون بالأقرار بذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defining silence as lack of useful argument may fit 77:35, but it gives no coherent meaning to this verse’s statement that no soul speaks except by God’s leave.
rows.anchor: وفيه إنه لو صح فإنما يصح في مثل قوله { هذا يوم لا ينطقون } وأما مثل قوله { يوم يأت لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } فلا يرجع إلى معنى محصل

rows.speaker: المرتضى
rows.claim: Al-Alūsī transmits from al-Murtaḍā’s Ghurar wa Durar that the long Resurrection day has periods when speech is barred and periods when it is allowed; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this conflicts with the verse’s apparent scope and repeats the stations problem.
rows.anchor: وقد يجاب كما نقله الآلوسي عن الغرر والدرر للمرتضى أن يوم القيامة يوم طويل ممتد فيجوز أن يمنعوا النطق في بعضه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some make the exception disconnected: humans cannot speak by their own power, while speech by God’s leave occurs; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī argues that all human acts always depend on God, so the meaningful distinction is between voluntary worldly speech and compelled speech in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ان الاستثناء في قوله { لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه } منقطع لا متصل أي لا تتكلم نفس باقتدار من عندها إلا بإذنه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Happiness is attaining the good that fulfills and pleases a person’s bodily and spiritual powers; misery is losing that good. In technical usage they are possession and privation, while good is broader than happiness.
rows.anchor: فسعادة كل شيء أن ينال ما لوجوده من الخير الذي يكمل بسببه ويلتذ به فهي في الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surface wording does not itself exclude a third class such as believers, unbelievers, and the unexposed or otherwise incapable; children and the insane are examples of the latter.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله تعالى { فمنهم شقي وسعيد } لا تفيد حصر أهل الجمع في الفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concerns everyone gathered on a witnessed Day that ends in Paradise or Fire, so the incapable are not left indefinitely waiting but ultimately join one of the two groups.
rows.anchor: ولا يدوم عليهم الحال بالإبهام والانتظار فهم بالآخرة ملحقون بإحدى الطائفتين السعداء أو الأشقياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the context makes the gathered people fall into the two outcomes, as in the other passage where context makes the Paradise and Fire groups exhaustive though the phrase alone does not.
rows.anchor: ولازم هذا السياق أن ينحصر أهل الجمع في الفريقين السعداء والأشقياء فما منهم إلا سعيد أو شقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not explain whether happiness and misery are intrinsic, fixed by an eternal will, or acquired by action; its setting of exhortation indicates that the path to happiness is made accessible.
rows.anchor: فلا نظر في الآية إلى شيء من ذلك غير أن وقوع الآية في سياق الدعوة إلى الإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that God’s present judgment and knowledge that some will be happy and others wretched make the outcome impossible to reverse, since reversal would make God’s report false and knowledge ignorant.
rows.anchor: ومن حكم الله عليه بحكم وعلم منه ذلك الأمر امتنع كونه بخلافه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar reports asking the Prophet whether people work on something already decreed; the Prophet answers that it is decreed, the pens are dry and fates have run, yet each person is facilitated toward what they were created for.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عمر أنه قال لما نزل قوله تعالى { فمنهم شقي وسعيد } قلت يا رسول الله فعلى ماذا نعمل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī reports the Muʿtazilite attribution to al-Ḥasan that people are wretched or happy through their own deeds; Rāzī replies that the deeds themselves occur by divine decree.
rows.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة روي عن الحسن أنه قال فمنهم شقي بعمله وسعيد بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls Rāzī’s proof a temporal equivocation: a truthful judgment now about a person’s future state does not make that state present now, just as a forecast does not bring its future event into the present.
rows.anchor: أما الذي سماه دليلا قاطعا فقد غالط فيه بأخذ زمان الحكم زمانا لنتيجته وأثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reports that people will be happy or wretched on the Resurrection Day, not that they have those states now or eternally; applying Rāzī’s argument consistently would make every future description hold before the Day as well.
rows.anchor: إن كان حكما بشقاوتهم وسعادتهم كذلك فإنما هو حكم صادر منه في هذا الآن بأنهم كذا وكذا يوم القيامة
